chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the mortgage (collateral) and the guarantor in a credit sale, so he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.الرَّهْن: Mortgage or collateral pledged to secure a debt
key_terms.الْكَفِيل: Guarantor who assumes responsibility for the debt
key_terms.بَيْعُ النَّسِيئَةِ: Sale on credit with deferred payment
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use both collateral and a guarantor in a credit sale according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of combining collateral (rahn) and a guarantor (kafil) in a credit sale (bai' al-nasi'ah) is affirmed, reflecting the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in securing deferred payments. This ruling aligns with the broader legal principle that multiple forms of security can coexist to mitigate risk in commercial transactions, provided they do not contradict the core elements of the contract. The Imam’s concise response underscores the ease with which such arrangements are integrated into Islamic trade law.
